title: Hydrodeoxygenation (HDO) of bio-oils reference family
reaction: Phenolics + n H2 -> arenes / cycloalkanes + n H2O (e.g., guaiacol -> phenol -> benzene; m-cresol -> toluene)
objective: Optional literature-backed family for hydrodeoxygenation of biomass-derived oxygenates (guaiacol, anisole, m-cresol, lignin phenols). Candidates compare a Pt / SiO2 noble-metal anchor (Resasco lab studies), a CoMoS sulfide commercial-style catalyst (lignin-to-arenes), and a NiMo / carbon non-noble emerging route.

balanced.label: Balanced
balanced.description: Balance catalyst cost, evidence quality, route maturity, and reported deoxygenation activity / aromatic preservation.

cost-first.label: Cost-first
cost-first.description: Bias ranking toward catalyst cost while preserving route and evidence guardrails.

evidence-first.label: Evidence-first
evidence-first.description: Reward stronger literature support and reproducible HDO routes.

citations.label: Catal. Today 2009
citations.note: Gutierrez, Kaila et al.: hydrodeoxygenation of guaiacol on noble-metal catalysts; foundational HDO benchmarking study (480+ citations) of Pt, Pd, Rh, Ru on Al2O3 and ZrO2.

citations.label: Energy Fuels 2011
citations.note: Gonzalez-Borja and Resasco: anisole and guaiacol HDO over monolithic Pt-Sn catalysts, showing how Sn promoter changes deoxygenation selectivity.

citations.label: J. Catal. 2014
citations.note: Nie and Resasco: kinetics and mechanism of m-cresol HDO on a Pt / SiO2 catalyst, providing transferable kinetic baselines for Pt-based HDO.

citations.label: Appl. Catal. A 2018
citations.note: Roldugina, Naranov et al.: HDO of guaiacol over mesoporous noble-metal catalysts in methanol, surveying Pt / Pd / Rh / Ru on different mesoporous supports.

citations.label: ACS Catal. 2018
citations.note: Song, Zhou et al.: surface engineering of CoMoS nanosulfide for HDO of lignin-derived phenols to arenes; key reference for the sulfide-based HDO route.

citations.label: ACS Catal. 2019
citations.note: Resasco and Yang: relationship between atomic-scale structure and reactivity of isolated Pt catalysts, focused on HDO of m-cresol.

citations.label: Green Chem. 2024
citations.note: Jiang, Shu et al.: efficient HDO of lignin-derived phenolic compounds under acid-free conditions over carbon-supported NiMo catalysts.

citations.label: Ind. Eng. Chem. Res. 2009
citations.note: Noble-metal HDO screening on real pyrolysis oil where Ru/C outperforms sulfided NiMo and CoMo.

citations.label: Energy Environ. Sci. 2010
citations.note: 5 wt% Ru/C at 350 C and 200 bar: oil yields to ~65 wt% and deoxygenation to 90 wt%.

route_templates.name: Pt / SiO2 HDO route
route_templates.manufacturing_mode: Supported Pt on silica HDO catalyst preparation
route_templates.route_note: Most transferable HDO basis for arene-preserving deoxygenation; Pt economics dominate.

route_templates.name: CoMoS sulfide HDO route
synthesis: Sequential or co-impregnation of Co / Mo
route_templates.route_note: CoMoS sulfide route mirrors industrial hydrotreating catalysts; route maturity is high but sulfidation control is demanding.

route_templates.name: NiMo / carbon non-noble HDO route
route_templates.manufacturing_mode: NiMo on carbon HDO catalyst preparation
synthesis: Sequential or co-impregnation of Ni / Mo
route_templates.route_note: NiMo on carbon non-noble HDO route, attractive when avoiding PGMs and operating sulfur-free is the program goal.

candidates.title: Pt / SiO2 HDO
candidates.summary: Pt on silica used as the canonical HDO benchmark for arene-preserving deoxygenation of guaiacol / anisole / m-cresol.
decision_notes: Best fit for arene-preserving HDO duty where Pt economics are acceptable.
Pt loading typically <2 wt% so support-cost share is meaningful relative to Pt.

pricing.note: Live Pt feed with a mild precursor / conversion markup for HDO Pt / SiO2 screening.
Silica support cost held on engineering proxy comparable to commercial silica gel ranges.

candidates.title: CoMoS / Al2O3 sulfide HDO
candidates.summary: CoMoS sulfide on alumina; the industrial hydrotreating-style HDO catalyst for lignin-derived phenol upgrading to arenes.
decision_notes: Best fit when industrial hydrotreating-style HDO is acceptable and sulfided-catalyst handling is in scope.
Sulfidation discipline (atmosphere, temperature ramp) drives long-hold activity.

pricing.note: Live Mo feed with a precursor / conversion markup; sulfide form derives from in-situ sulfidation.
Live Co feed with a precursor / conversion markup.

Gamma-alumina support cost held on engineering proxy. USGS MCS 2026 metallurgical alumina (2025e $590/t import value, ~$0.27/lb) is the public floor; catalyst-grade premium retained. UN Comtrade 2024: calcined alumina (HS 281820) averaged $0.60/kg with specialty flows to $3.64/kg; catalyst-carrier activated/gamma alumina marketplace offers run $800-1,700/t.

candidates.title: NiMo / carbon (acid-free)
candidates.summary: NiMo on carbon for acid-free HDO of lignin phenols, a non-noble option that avoids alumina acidity and sulfur handling.
decision_notes: Best fit when avoiding noble metals and sulfide handling is the program goal.
NiMo / carbon trades sulfide-route maturity for cleaner reduction chemistry; activity is competitive with sulfides on selected substrates.

pricing.note: Live Mo feed with a precursor / conversion markup.
Live Ni feed with a precursor / conversion markup.

pricing.evidence_label: UN Comtrade activated-carbon import unit value
pricing.note: 2024 U.S. imports of HS 380210: $240.27M / 88.93M kg = $2.70/kg CIF average.

candidates.title: Ru/C noble-metal route
candidates.summary: Five percent ruthenium on activated carbon upgrades real pyrolysis oil at 350 C and 200 bar to ~65 wt% oil yield with 90 wt% deoxygenation, beating the sulfide baselines without sulfur management.
decision_notes: The sulfur-free premium option proven on real (not model) bio-oil; ruthenium inventory is the whole cost story.
Rides the family's existing carbon-impregnation route.

pricing.note: Live Ru feed with a precursor markup; 5 wt% loading is source-quoted.

pricing.evidence_label: UN Comtrade activated-carbon import unit value
pricing.note: 2024 U.S. imports of HS 380210: $2.70/kg CIF average.
